papers.title: CT-based 3D morphometric reference data on osseous TMJ subunits in a European cohort: relevance for patient-specific implant research
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Patient-specific alloplastic prostheses are increasingly used for reconstruction of the temporomandibular joint (TMJ). However, the extent to which articulating implant components should reflect native osseous TMJ morphology remains unresolved. This study used CT-derived three-dimensional (3D) virtual-digital surface models to analyze osseous TMJ subunits in humans and provide morphometric reference data for future patient-specific TMJ implant research. Methods In this retrospective exploratory study, 97 computed tomography (CT) scans from Hannover Medical School were analyzed. High-quality 3D virtual-digital models of the articulating TMJ subunits, including the mandibular condyle and glenoid fossa, were generated and used to measure relevant TMJ parameters. Parameters were compared according to sex and age, and correlation analyses were performed. Results Morphometric variability was observed among the osseous TMJ subunits. Men showed larger medial-lateral diameters of the mandibular condyle, greater articular tubercle height, and larger zygomatic arch root dimensions. Women showed a larger anterior-posterior diameter of the glenoid fossa. Middle-aged participants showed a larger anterior-posterior diameter of the mandibular condyle and larger sagittal dimensions of the zygomatic arch root compared with young-aged participants. Correlation analysis revealed associations between selected parameters, particularly between zygomatic arch root diameter and articular tubercle height. Conclusion This study provides CT-based 3D morphometric reference data on osseous TMJ subunits in a European cohort. The findings indicate inter-individual morphometric variability and exploratory sex- and age-related differences in selected parameters. These data may provide anatomical reference information for future patient-specific TMJ implant research. However, the present study does not evaluate implant fit, mandibular kinematics, biomechanical performance, or clinical outcomes. Therefore, the translational relevance of these findings requires further validation.

papers.title: Femoral de-escalation during revision total hip arthroplasty using a rectangular-taper shortened stem
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose Long stems with diaphyseal fixation are widely used in revision total hip arthroplasty (RTHA) but may increase surgical complexity and compromise femoral bone stock. Primary femoral stems, used as a de-escalation strategy, could simplify RTHA in selected patients as a bone preserving strategy. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical and radiographic outcomes of this technique using a cementless rectangular-taper shortened stem during both components RTHA. Methods Between January 2019 and January 2025, 301 both components RTHA were prospectively included in our institutional total joint registry. Among them, 23 RTHA (20 patients, 14 men, mean age at revision = 63 years [54–71]) with femoral de-escalation with the use of a cementless rectangular-taper shortened stem and a dual mobility cup construct were identified and retrospectively reviewed at latest follow-up, focusing on complications related to this reconstruction technique. Clinical outcome was evaluated with the Harris Hip Score (HHS). Results At a mean follow-up of 48 months (23–75), no postoperative periprosthetic fracture, mechanical failure or early loosening of the femoral reconstruction occurred. One early dislocation occurred at 41 days, managed by closed reduction without recurrence at latest follow-up. The mean HHS significantly improved from 70 (59–83) preoperatively to 94 (64–100) postoperatively, with 96% of patients achieving HHS ≥ 80 at latest follow-up. Conclusions In selected patients undergoing RTHA with limited femoral bone loss, femoral de-escalation with a cementless rectangular-taper shortened stem demonstrated reliability for femoral reconstruction with no component-related complication and significant functional improvement at short-term follow-up.

papers.title: From Measured Accuracy to Patient Outcome: Navigation in Total Hip Arthroplasty and Molecular Diagnosis of Periprosthetic Joint Infection: A Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Background: Total hip arthroplasty (THA) and the diagnosis of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) have each acquired a technology that measures with high precision: intraoperative navigation, which reports component position to within a few degrees, and molecular methods, which identify the infecting organism and the host response at genomic resolution. Objective: To establish whether the measured accuracy has been shown to reach the patient as a clinical outcome. Methods: This is a narrative review, reported according to SANRA. MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science databases were searched from inception to 31 August 2026. English-language studies in humans were eligible if they reported positional or diagnostic accuracy, a patient-level clinical or economic outcome after THA or after treatment of PJI or osteomyelitis, or a factor modifying the relation between the two. Animal, in vitro, and cadaveric studies, conference abstracts, and reports without extractable data were excluded. Forty studies were included. No pooled estimate was calculated, and no new statistical analysis was performed. Results: Navigation reduced positional outliers consistently, but in two matched claims-based cohorts of patients with morbid obesity (4499 and 5835 patients), it was not associated with lower rates of PJI, dislocation, periprosthetic fracture, mechanical loosening, or revision within two years. Candidate immunogenetic variants in osteomyelitis have never been tested against a treatment decision. Metagenomic sequencing was no more accurate than culture (sensitivity 63.2% versus 68.4%; specificity 80.0% versus 95.0%) except after antibiotic exposure. Reported infection rates and test accuracy both change with the case definition applied. Conclusions: In both settings, the limiting factor is the design of the studies linking measurement to outcome rather than the precision of the measurement.

papers.title: A multilevel multi-objective surrogate-based optimization of a UAV wing considering structural and aerodynamic performances
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a generic approach for the shape optimization and structural sizing of fixed-wing UAV wings. This approach is multidisciplinary, integrating aerodynamic and structural analyses through a one-way coupling suitable for preliminary design. The aerodynamic analysis is performed using the panel method, while structural analysis is carried out using the finite element method. The optimal design problem, aiming to find the shape and dimensions of the structure that minimize wing weight and maximize Lift-to-Drag Ratio, is formulated as a multi-objective problem and solved using the NSGA-II algorithm. The multidisciplinarity and large number of design variables are managed through a multi-level approach: for each shape configuration, structural sizing is performed using the Fully Stressed Design (FSD) method. Surrogate Based Optimization (SBO) is used to efficiently solve the problem. The Predator MQ-1 drone wing was chosen as a case study. The optimization results demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Comparison of a Parametric Physics-Informed Neural Network and a Tensorial Reduced-Order Model for the Shallow-Water Dam-Break Problem
papers.abstract: We develop two parametric data-driven reduced models: a physics-informed neural network (PINN) and a non-intrusive tensorial reduced-order model (TROM), and apply both approaches to the parametrized one-dimensional shallow-water dam-break problem. Both reduced models do not require time integration and learn a direct solution map from space, time, and dam-break parameters to the physical state. We present a detailed comparison for out-of-sample and extrapolated parameter values. In addition, we demonstrate that it is essential to introduce shock-aware collocation to improve the robustness of the PINN model.

papers.title: Edge effects on the pressure drop through triply periodic minimal surface heat exchangers
papers.abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) geometries offer significant potential for compact, high-performance heat exchangers, but confinement-induced edge effects in small-scale test articles can distort the measured pressure drop and its extrapolation to full-scale performance. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first combined experimental and CFD study to vary the number of complete transverse unit cells, from 1 × 1 to 6 × 6, inside a square enclosure while the Diamond TPMS unit cell topology, its orientation and phase, the nominal wall thickness, and the streamwise length are held fixed. Pressure drop was measured with air ( Re = 220–7290) and simulated with CFD ( Re up to 8000); mean absolute differences are 1.4 to 5.6% for the 1 × 1 through 4 × 4 and 8.8% for the 6 × 6 and 13.7% for the 5 × 5. For Re = 3000–8000, the ratio of each pressure gradient to an extrapolated bulk limit collapses onto one exponential decay with cell count, with a mean absolute error of 0.040. The fitted confinement penalty relative to the extrapolated bulk limit is 150% at 1 × 1 and 12% at 6 × 6. CFD-based flow-field visualization illustrates the mechanism: corner recirculation behind rearward-facing lattice peaks and high-velocity channeling through diagonally opposing forward-facing corners, whose share of the cross-section shrinks as the cell count grows. The fitted relation predicts a confinement penalty below 5% at eight or more cells across. This threshold lies beyond the tested range. The relation is specific to the studied Diamond geometry, but the mechanism is a transferable framework for interpreting sub-scale TPMS test data.

papers.title: Decision-making and planning for autonomous vehicles on foggy highway obstacle sections under visual perception
papers.abstract: To enhance the safety and decision reliability of automated driving vehicles on foggy highway obstacle sections, this study addresses three key challenges: visual perception degradation, increased uncertainty in obstacle localization, and trajectory instability under high-speed conditions. A decision-making and planning method specifically designed for foggy scenarios is proposed. The method constructs a visual perception degradation model grounded in atmospheric scattering theory, and introduces uncertainty-inflated occupancy sets alongside blind-zone virtual occupancy sets to impose unified constraints on both visible and unobservable regions. An adaptive triggering mechanism is developed based on fog-effective time-to-collision, candidate behaviors are screened using velocity-adaptive terminal-state sampling, and trajectory optimization with collision avoidance control is accomplished via variable-step nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) framework. The proposed method is validated across three dimensions: varying vehicle speeds, fog intensity levels, and representative obstacle scenarios. Results demonstrate that the method achieves stable, conservative, and executable closed-loop decision-making and planning under perception-limited conditions, simultaneously improving collision avoidance success rate, trajectory smoothness, and state convergence while maintaining real-time performance.

papers.title: Predicting Lentil Seed Yield from Agronomic Traits Using a Foundation-Augmented Machine Learning Ensemble
papers.abstract: Accurate agricultural yield prediction is crucial for crop management and data-driven decision-making. This study proposes a machine learning framework for predicting total lentil seed yield using 264 observations collected during a single growing season at one location in Sivas, Türkiye. Seven regression models and the tabular foundation model TabPFN were evaluated through nested cross-validation. The fixed post hoc Foundation-Augmented Averaging Ensemble (FAAE) combined TabPFN, Extra Trees, CatBoost, and XGBoost using equal weights, while the primary fully nested evaluation selected the four ensemble members within each outer training fold. The fully nested FAAE achieved R2 = 0.891 ± 0.045, comparable to the strongest individual models, while the fixed post hoc FAAE yielded R2 = 0.897 ± 0.038. Split conformal prediction produced well-calibrated uncertainty intervals at 80%, 90%, and 95% coverage. SHAP and LOCO identified pods per plant and biological yield as the dominant predictors of lentil yield. Overall, these findings indicate that FAAE can provide competitive predictive performance within a leakage-controlled framework while also supporting uncertainty quantification and biologically meaningful interpretation. Because the dominant predictors, pods per plant and biological yield, are measured at or near physiological maturity, the proposed framework is more suitable for end-of-season yield estimation than for early-season forecasting. The framework therefore shows potential for within-trial yield assessment, although validation using replicated material across additional years and locations is required before broader generalization.

papers.abstract: Abstract This study optimizes the Laser Powder Bed Fusion (L-PBF) parameters for AISI 316 L stainless steel using a Central Composite Design (CCD) and Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to evaluate the effects of laser power, scanning speed, and hatching strategy on tensile mechanical responses. The scanning strategy is treated as an explicit categorical factor within the response surfaces, which allows its effect to be tested by ANOVA on the same footing as the continuous factors. ANOVA confirmed laser power and scanning speed as the most critical non-linear factors, with the optimized 0/90 strategy maximizing stiffness and strength. The predictive models exhibited high adequacy ( $$R^{2}_{\textrm{adj}} > 93\%$$ , non-significant lack-of-fit, and absolute prediction errors below 3.1% across the design space). Multi-objective optimization via NSGA-II and TOPSIS converged to a highly stable processing window: laser power between 168.8 W and 169.7 W, scanning speed of 717.2 mm/s, and the optimized 0/90 strategy. This optimal condition predicts an elastic modulus of 174.2 GPa, a yield strength of 498.9 MPa, and a strength coefficient of 673.2 MPa, representing gains of up to 35.0% over the poorest experimental condition. Experimental validation yielded relative errors below 8.3%, and Monte Carlo simulations ( $$n = 5000$$ ) confirmed substantial robustness with coefficients of variation strictly under 0.16%.

papers.title: Sequence-Conditioned Physics-Informed Neural Network for Lithium-Ion Battery State of Health Estimation Using Charging Segments at High State of Charge
papers.abstract: Accurate and reliable state of health (SOH) estimation is essential for lithium-ion battery safety and lifetime management. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) integrate battery degradation knowledge with deep learning to improve the physical consistency of SOH estimation. However, existing PINNs insufficiently capture degradation evolution across consecutive cycles and show limited applicability across battery chemistries and charge/discharge protocols. To address these issues, we propose a sequence-conditioned physics-informed neural network (SC-PINN) that uses a gated recurrent unit (GRU) to encode local degradation states and incorporates a degradation dynamics consistency constraint and a monotonic degradation prior to improve prediction accuracy and physical plausibility. We also develop a general charging feature extraction method for different battery chemistries and charge/discharge protocols, extracting unified 18-dimensional health features from charging segments at high state of charge (SOC). The method is validated using 317 batteries and 197,024 valid cycle samples covering four battery chemistries across nine representative tasks. SC-PINN achieves a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.6285% and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.8924%, with the lowest RMSE in eight of nine tasks. Compared with other methods, the proposed method demonstrates good stability and applicability in both standard and small-sample experiments.

papers.abstract: Abstract This paper is presenting a systematic approach for designing of antenna resonating at 3.18 GHz with an impedance bandwidth of 3.10–3.285 GHz which lies at the lower edge of the UWB spectrum used in IEEE 802.15.6-based Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) research. The proposed compact antenna becomes more suitable for WBAN-assisted healthcare monitoring and microwave biomedical sensing applications. The antenna designing is covered in two sections. First one deals with the non-linear regression analysis with correlation analysis to achieve final design for patch. The surrogate modelling for reflection coefficient parameter for complete 50 samples of the patch design is presented and compared with other techniques. The non-linear regression based surrogate modelling along with correlation analysis by Pearson and Spearman techniques helps in making prediction of the patch design structure by selecting most featured and significant design parameters. The second section caters the process of ‘Artificial Neural Network (ANN)’ modelling with optimization techniques to achieve optimized design of ‘Defected Ground Structure (DGS)’ structure. The optimization is performed by ‘Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II)’, Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO)’, ‘Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO)’, and ‘Bayesian Optimization using Gaussian Process Regression (BO + GPR)’ techniques. The optimized antenna having size of $$0.2968 {\lambda}_{0} \text{m}\text{m} \times 0.318 {\lambda}_{0} \text{m}\text{m}$$ at resonant frequency of 3.18 GHz, is fabricated on FR-4 substrate. The excellent agreement is observed between simulated results and practical results which confirms the robustness of the proposed systematic approach for the antenna designing and making it suitable for biomedical application.

papers.abstract: This research aims to: 1) draft a supervision model by network partners to develop pre-service teachers through a professional learning community; 2) develop a supervision model by network partners to develop pre-service teachers through a professional learning community; and 3) evaluate the use of the supervision model by network partners to develop pre-service teachers through a professional learning community. This research is a mixed-methods study. The research methodology was divided into three phases: Phase 1, drafting a supervision model by network partners to develop pre-service teachers through a professional learning community, involving 9 experts as informants. Focus group discussions were the research tool, and data were analyzed using content analysis. The research findings revealed that the supervision model by network partners to develop pre-service teachers through a professional learning community comprises: 1) principles of the model, 2) objectives of the model, 3) content of the model, 4) measurement and evaluation of the model, and 5) conditions for the model's success. Phase 2, developing a supervision model by network partners to develop pre-service teachers through a professional learning community. 9 experts provided input to evaluate the model. The evaluation tool used was an assessment of the model's propriety, feasibility, and utility. Statistical analysis included the mean and standard deviation. The research findings indicated that the propriety, feasibility, and utility of the model were at the highest level. Phase 3 evaluated the use of the supervision model by network partners to develop pre-service teachers through a professional learning community. The process involves: 1) the model was implemented with 3 pre-service teachers; 2) the informants consisted of 12 network partners, including lecturers, school administrators, mentor teachers, and educational supervisors; and 3) seven experts evaluated the model. The research instruments consisted of a behavioral and learning management competency observation form, a pre-service teachers’ competency evaluation form, and a model implementation evaluation form. The statistics used for data analysis were the mean and standard deviation, and content analysis. The research results are as follows: 1) observations of all three pre-service teachers showed significant improvement in their competencies in planning and designing learning management, organizing active learning activities, selecting and using media and technology, classroom management, and measuring and evaluating learning outcomes. The improvement progressed from basic learning management skills in the first session to higher-quality learning management in the second session. 2) The results of the pre-service teachers’ competencies assessment were at the highest level. 3) The results of the assessment of the model's utility were at the highest level.

papers.title: Physically Constrained Temporal Fusion Transformer with LLM-Assisted Hyperparameter Optimization for Multi-Scenario Energy Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Accurate forecasting of battery state of health (SOH), wind power, and photovoltaic (PV) power is challenged by non-stationarity, multiscale dependencies, and physically implausible outputs. This study proposes a physically constrained Temporal Fusion Transformer (PC-TFT) that coordinates enhanced temporal representation, physical regularization, and LLM-assisted Bayesian optimization. Mogrifier-LSTM and a feature-enhanced attention module capture transient fluctuations and long-range dependencies, while spectral normalization stabilizes training under physical constraints. Scenario-specific differentiable penalties discourage unrealistic battery SOH rebounds, wind-power boundary violations, and inconsistent PV irradiance–power relationships. An LLM incorporates domain knowledge to refine the hyperparameter search space, while numerical optimization determines the final configuration. Experiments on three energy datasets show that, relative to the standard TFT, PC-TFT reduces RMSE by 62.7%, 13.8%, and 15.8% for battery SOH, wind-power, and photovoltaic-power forecasting, respectively, while achieving R2 values above 0.97. These results demonstrate improvements in forecasting accuracy and physical consistency across the evaluated datasets, highlighting the potential of PC-TFT for forecasting-assisted energy management.

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Risk-Guided Active Learning for Malware Concept Drift Adaptation
papers.abstract: Mobile malware evolution induces concept drift, degrading the performance of static supervised detectors. Concept Drift Adaptation with Active Learning (CDA-AL) mitigates this problem by querying informative samples for model updating, but existing methods still face two limitations. First, uncertainty-based selection measures prediction ambiguity without explicitly assessing consistency with previously learned representation structure, causing confidently misclassified drifted samples to be overlooked. Second, conventional retraining often treats labeled samples uniformly, providing insufficient emphasis on missed malware and samples near ambiguous benign-malicious boundaries. To address these limitations, we propose GRAD (Geometry-Aware Risk-Guided Active Drift Adaptation), a CDA-AL framework with three complementary modules. Geometry-Aware Drift-Risk Ranking uses residual deviations from locally estimated benign tangent spaces to prioritize potential misclassification risks. Hybrid active sample selection combines geometry-ranked risk candidates with uncertainty sampling under a fixed annotation budget. Boundary-Aware Retraining constructs Error Memory and Semantic Ambiguity Memory and applies targeted triplet constraints to correct missed malware and improve class separation. Experiments on two large-scale temporal malware datasets totaling over 460K samples show that GRAD achieves the best F1 performance on both datasets, improving F1 by 3.26% on APIGraph and 7.23% on AndroZoo, while reducing FNR by 39.15% and FPR by 72.50%, respectively. GRAD also shows no evidence of systematic catastrophic forgetting and reduces the number of long-lived malware samples by 12.5% on APIGraph.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Neural Networks for Latent-Driven Non-Gaussian Outputs
papers.abstract: Uncertainty quantification (UQ) is essential for reliable predictions in artificial neural networks when latent sources of randomness produce non-Gaussian outputs for a given deterministic input. We propose UQ-ANN, a data-driven framework composed of two coupled subnetworks. The first subnetwork contains two feedforward neural networks: ANN1 predicts the conditional mean and ANN2 the conditional covariance of a reduced representation obtained by principal component analysis (PCA) of the outputs. The second subnetwork is an analytical stochastic generator and requires no training. It is based on a sparse Gaussian kernel density estimator (GKDE) constructed by adaptive clustering. The sparsification replaces the kernels associated with the training points by a reduced set of cluster-based kernels, while third- and fourth-moment descriptors are included in the merging criterion to preserve non-Gaussian features. Independent realizations in the reduced space are then generated, transformed to reproduce the conditional mean and covariance predicted by the first subnetwork, and mapped back to the original output space. They provide conditional statistics, conditional probability density functions, and conditional prediction intervals. A marginal log-density diagnostic is also used to assess the stochastic approximation. Numerical tests on synthetic datasets evaluate the sparse GKDE, the stochastic generator, and the complete UQ-ANN framework, including out-of-sample predictions.

papers.title: Topology‐porosity assessment of TPMS ‐based aluminum foams for accelerated melting of RT31 phase change material
papers.abstract: Abstract Thermal energy storage systems based on phase change materials are limited by the low thermal conductivity of PCMs, which results in slow melting and temperature non‐uniformity. In this study, a three‐dimensional numerical investigation was performed to assess the combined effects of TPMS ( Triply Periodic Minimal Surface ) topology and porosity on the melting behavior of RT31 PCM. Gyroid, Schwarz Diamond, and Schwarz Primitive structures were examined using the enthalpy‐porosity method in ANSYS Fluent R19. The numerical model showed good agreement with the experimental RT31 data, with an RMSE of 1.24°C and an of 0.995. At the common porosity of 85.11%, the Gyroid configuration reached 95% melting in 57.29 s, compared with 100.89 s for Schwarz Diamond and 99.91 s for Schwarz Primitive, corresponding to reductions of 43.2% and 42.7%, respectively. For the Gyroid topology, decreasing porosity from 92.03% to 78.18% reduced the time to 95% melting from 65.76 to 50.32 s, an improvement of approximately 23.5%. However, lower porosity also reduced PCM volume and restricted natural convection. The results therefore show that intermediate Gyroid porosities provide the most balanced compromise between rapid melting, thermal uniformity, natural‐convection development, and latent storage capacity.

papers.title: Delay-Compensated MPC for Path Tracking of Articulated Steering Vehicles
papers.abstract: Abstract Articulated steering vehicles are key equipment for mining transportation, underground roadways, and heavy-duty material handling infrastructure, where insufficient path-tracking accuracy may reduce roadway safety margins and increase the risk of lane encroachment, collision, and traffic interruption in confined haulage corridors. Hydraulic actuator delay is a practical source of steering lag in such vehicles, but it is often simplified or neglected in existing path-tracking control studies. To address this gap, this study develops a delay-compensated model predictive control (MPC) framework by incorporating experimentally identified hydraulic actuator delay into the pre‍dictive control model. Simulation results showed that MPC provided better stability performance than linear quadratic regulator (LQR), reducing sideslip angle, yaw rate, and lateral acceleration by 21%–48% under representative lane-change maneuvers. With actuator-delay compensation, the proposed MPC further reduced the tractor lateral deviation by 53.12% under single lane change (SLC) and 83.63% under double lane change (DLC) conditions. These results indicate that the proposed method can improve the operational safety, tracking reliability, and automation readiness of articulated vehicles used in mining and infrastructure transportation scenarios.

papers.title: Robust Model Predictive Control of a Drum Boiler with Online Uncertainty Estimation
papers.abstract: In drum boiler control, model predictive control can provide accurate tracking under constraints, but residual model uncertainty still causes safety violations when parameters drift. Purpose. The study developed a robust model predictive controller for a drum boiler in which the safety margin is adjusted online according to the uncertainty level. Methods. А Takagi—Sugeno model with recursive least squares parameter adaptation described the nonlinear plant. Uncertainty was estimated from two sources: the covariance of the identified parameters and a sliding window of prediction errors. The combined estimate tightened output constraints and adjusted control smoothing. The robust layer does not require robust invariant set computation. Results. Numerical experiments on a drum boiler model compared four controller configurations during a 3000-step scenario with three phases of parameter drift. The configuration that combined model adaptation with the robust layer reduced the integral absolute error by 58.3 percent and reduced the number of constraint violations by 47.8 percent relative to the nominal controller. The maximum violation magnitude decreased by 33.8 percent. The configuration with the robust layer alone achieved the smallest number of violations, although it produced less accurate tracking. The average computation time per control step was 2.6 ms. Practical relevance. The proposed algorithm can be integrated into an existing predictive controller as a lightweight safety layer for thermal power equipment. Discussion. The results support the joint use of online identification and adaptive safety margins; future work should address multi-step uncertainty propagation and experimental validation on hardware.

papers.title: Analyzing the Performance of Improved Feature-Based Active Learning Model for Audio-Based Speaker Identification
papers.abstract: Speaker identification systems must achieve high recognition performance while reducing the dependence on large labelled speech datasets and excessive computational resources. This study presents an Improved Feature-Based Active Learning Model (IFALM) for audio-based speaker identification. The proposed framework uses acoustic speech characteristics as the primary input and combines feature extraction, active sample selection, and CNN-based speaker classification. An uncertainty- and diversity-aware active learning technique is used to choose informative speech samples from the unlabeled pool, allowing the model to prioritise examples that are anticipated to enhance speaker-discriminative learning. The proposed approach is evaluated using the TIMIT and VoxCeleb1 speech datasets. While the VoxCeleb1 experiment achieves an accuracy of 82.90% under the predetermined training and testing regimen, the experimental findings show a mean speaker-identification accuracy of 98.26% and an equal error rate of 1.92% on TIMIT. The results indicate that the proposed active-learning framework can maintain competitive speaker-identification performance while improving the efficiency of labelled-data utilization. The present study focuses exclusively on acoustic speech-based speaker identification. No visual or facial information, audiovisual or multimodal fusion, speaker diarization, or downstream natural language processing tasks are implemented or evaluated.

papers.title: Pedagogical Foundations of Active Learning: Rethinking Teaching Approaches for the Next Generation of Educators
papers.abstract: Active learning is widely promoted to enhance learner participation and meaningful learning, yet its conceptualization remains fragmented across instructional techniques, engagement processes, teacher roles, and emerging technological contexts. This conceptual article reconsiders active learning as a coherent pedagogical orientation and develops an integrative account of its pedagogical foundations for the next generation of educators. Drawing on a thematic synthesis of relevant literature, the article identifies interconnected dimensions comprising pedagogical purpose, meaningful learning activity, cognitive engagement, teacher facilitation, learner agency, feedback, relational conditions, and digital/AI environments. The synthesis positions cognitive engagement as a central mechanism through which purposeful activities contribute to meaningful learning, while teacher facilitation and learning conditions sustain this process. The resulting framework conceptualizes active learning as a dynamic, interdependent, and recursive pedagogical system, rather than a linear sequence or collection of techniques. Digital and AI technologies are positioned as contextual pedagogical affordances whose value depends on purposeful integration and critical use. The framework repositions teachers as pedagogical designers and facilitators who orchestrate learning conditions while sustaining learner agency. This conceptualization provides a coherent foundation for understanding active learning and preparing educators to design meaningful, learner-centered environments responsive to contemporary educational demands.

papers.abstract: Background: This randomized controlled trial investigated whether adding a visual feedback-based (VFB) rehabilitation program to standard care could enhance gait performance and pelvic kinematics in patients recovering from total hip arthroplasty (THA). Methods: Inpatients aged 55 to 80 years who underwent unilateral THA by a lateral approach were randomized to either a VFB group or a control group. The VFB group received 30 minutes of technology-assisted visual feedback training using TecnoBody systems plus 30 minutes of conventional physiotherapy daily, while the control group received one hour of conventional therapy alone, both 5 days per week for 6 weeks. Gait and pelvic kinematics were assessed using the G-WALK inertial sensor at baseline and after 6 weeks, alongside clinical measures for pain, functional independence, and ambulation capacity. Results: Both groups showed significant improvements on clinical scales, with no meaningful differences between them. However, the VFB group demonstrated significantly greater gains in key gait and kinematic parameters, including cadence, speed, symmetry, pelvic tilt, and pelvic obliquity, with multivariate analysis confirming a distinct and more favorable post-treatment kinematic profile. Conclusion: Incorporating visual feedback-based training into postoperative rehabilitation after THA leads to superior improvements in gait quality and pelvic control compared with conventional therapy alone, supporting its clinical integration in standard physiotherapy programs. papers.title: Bayesian and probit comparative analysis of factors associated with blood pressure status among adults in the Kassena-Nankana Districts, Ghana: an AWI-Gen sub-study
papers.abstract: Hypertension prevalence is rising in rural Ghana, but the comparative behaviour of frequentist and Bayesian inferential frameworks for ordinal blood pressure outcomes in this setting remains underexamined. This study applied both frequentist (ordered probit) and Bayesian ordered probit models to identify factors associated with blood pressure status and to compare the two frameworks on coefficient agreement, uncertainty quantification, and model fit. This was a cross-sectional analysis of 2,010 adults aged 40–60 years in the Kassena-Nankana districts. Blood pressure was classified into four ordinal categories (Normal, Elevated, Stage 1, Stage 2 hypertension) per ACC/AHA 2017 thresholds. A directed acyclic graph informed a minimal adjustment set of age, sex, marital status, occupation, smoking, alcohol use, pesticide exposure, body mass index, and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity. Ordered probit models were fitted under frequentist and Bayesian (Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, weakly informative priors, four chains) frameworks on the complete-case analytic sample ( n = 1,979). The proportional-odds assumption was assessed with the Brant test. Model fit was compared using AIC (frequentist) and Pareto-smoothed importance-sampling leave-one-out cross-validation (Bayesian), placed on a commensurable deviance scale. The distribution of blood pressure category was Normal 46.1%, Elevated 12.4%, Stage 1 hypertension 19.6%, and Stage 2 hypertension 21.9% (combined Stage 1/Stage 2: 41.5%). Older age (probit β = 0.032 per year, 95% CI 0.023–0.041; Bayesian mean 0.032, 95% CrI 0.023–0.041), male sex (probit β = 0.279, 95% CI 0.141–0.417; Bayesian mean 0.279, 95% CrI 0.137–0.420), and higher BMI (probit β = 0.054, 95% CI 0.039–0.069; Bayesian mean 0.054, 95% CrI 0.039–0.069) were consistently associated with higher blood pressure category in both frameworks. The Brant test indicated that the sex association was not constant across severity thresholds (χ2 = 10.78, df = 2, p = 0.005), while all other covariates were consistent with proportional odds. Married status (probit β = -0.129, 95% CI -0.240 to -0.018) and pesticide exposure (probit β = -0.122, 95% CI -0.225 to -0.019) were each inversely associated with blood pressure category in both frameworks. Current smoking showed a negative but non-significant association (probit β = -0.119, 95% CI -0.264 to 0.025, p = 0.106). Frequentist and Bayesian coefficients agreed to within 0.001–0.002 across all predictors, and model fit was comparable on a commensurable scale (frequentist AIC = 4,936.5; Bayesian − 2×elpd_loo = 4,937.3; difference = 0.8). Older age, male sex, and higher BMI were robust factors associated with blood pressure category in this population, though the sex association varies in magnitude across severity thresholds. The inverse associations with married status and pesticide exposure are unexpected and are best interpreted as hypothesis-generating given the cross-sectional design. Frequentist and Bayesian ordered probit models produced materially equivalent inference once the adjustment set and data quality were addressed, indicating that framework choice is secondary to rigorous data preparation in this setting.

papers.title: Robust collapse prediction for corroded subsea pipelines under multiaxial loading: A physics-informed Bayesian framework constrained by symbolic regression
papers.abstract: Subsea pipeline collapse under multiaxial loads and corrosion severely threatens offshore structural integrity. This study introduces an integrated FE-SR-PINN-BNN framework, combining detailed 3D finite element (FE) numerical modeling in ABAQUS with a physics-informed Bayesian neural network (PINN-BNN) constrained by symbolic regression (SR). Explicit algebraic expressions of underlying mechanical mechanisms derived via SR are embedded into the PINN-BNN loss function as structural physics constraints. Numerical results show that the proposed model achieves a high coefficient of determination (R 2 = 0.9940) with prediction residuals within ±1.5 MPa, significantly outperforming purely data-driven machine learning models and empirical formula-constrained physics-informed baselines. In robustness evaluations with 5%-20% added noise, its R 2 performance degrades by only 33.49%, substantially lower than benchmark model drops. Under an extreme small-sample evaluation using only 10% training data, its R 2 reaches 0.8464, outperforming four purely data-driven baselines by 97.99%, 42.18%, 39.44%, and 8.35%, respectively. Beyond precise collapse pressure predictions, the framework incorporates uncertainty quantification based on 95% prediction intervals, achieving a mean prediction interval width of 1.88 MPa and a coverage probability of 0.952, exceptionally close to the theoretical 0.95 target. This study provides reliable support for structural integrity and safety assessment of subsea pipelines in complex service environments.

papers.title: Adaptive threshold optimization for efficient and robust high-dimensional sensor calibration in building energy systems
papers.abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and big data technologies, high-quality data have become increasingly essential for effective building energy system management. High-dimensional in-situ calibration provides a promising way to correct sensor biases in building energy systems without relying on physical reference sensors. However, practical applications face significant challenges due to random measurement noise and the computational burden of high-dimensional data. To address these issues, this study proposes a sensor in-situ calibration framework integrated with Bayesian optimization, referred to as SIC-BO. In the proposed framework, a Gaussian probability-based confidence evaluation method is first developed to quantify sensor credibility under physical and semi-physical constraints. Sensors with low confidence are then selected as calibration candidates, thereby reducing calibration dimensionality and improving practical identifiability. Bayesian optimization is further employed to adaptively determine the sensor-confidence threshold and objective-function threshold, so that solution stability and computational efficiency can be balanced without empirical trial. The proposed method was validated using a chiller plant system in a commercial building in Hong Kong. Across five fault scenarios with different fault scales and random-error levels, the selected calibration solutions achieved system-level MAPE values below 2%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SIC-BO in improving calibration stability and computational efficiency under different fault and noise conditions within chiller plant systems.

papers.title: Real-time reconstruction of the internal temperature field of welding using global physics-mixed long short-term memory network and physical constraint reconstruction
papers.abstract: Accurate reconstruction of internal welding temperature fields is essential for evaluating thermal cycles and weld quality, yet direct internal measurement is difficult. This study proposes a real-time reconstruction framework for the internal temperature field of SUS304 gas metal arc welding (GMAW) butt joints by coupling a physics-constrained mixed deep operator network (PMix-DeepONet) predictor with spatio-temporal physics-augmented plate spline interpolation (ST-PAS). In PMix-DeepONet, a global physics-mixed long short-term memory (Mix-LSTM) encoder performs physical mixing of welding current, voltage, surface molten-pool temperature, and temporal information before recurrent encoding, enabling the branch network to capture multi-source process dynamics. The DeepONet branch-trunk operator-learning structure then maps the encoded process features and spatiotemporal coordinates to the internal temperature field, while heat-transfer, boundary-condition, initial-condition, and high-temperature-sensitive constraints guide the prediction toward physically meaningful solutions. ST-PAS further combines an adaptively fitted Goldak-like thermal-shape prior with residual plate-spline correction to refine sparse reconstructed fields while preserving nonlinear heat-field morphology. Experiments show that PMix-DeepONet reduces the overall root mean square error (RMSE) from 35.78 °C to 22.09 °C compared with DeepONet. In the high-temperature region above 1000 °C, the RMSE decreases from 66.78 °C to 23.71 °C. Ablation results confirm the importance of Mix-LSTM and physical constraints for stable high-gradient prediction. For spatial refinement, ST-PAS achieves the lowest RMSE of 57.90 °C and MSE of 3352.05, reducing RMSE and MSE by 1.09% and 2.18% compared with LSM-SP. Qualitative comparisons further verify the effectiveness of the framework for real-time SUS304 GMAW temperature-field prediction.

papers.title: Physics-informed learning of health-aware equivalent circuit parameter evolution for lithium-ion batteries
papers.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries exhibit nonlinear degradation under complex operating conditions and long-term cycling. Existing studies mainly focus on state-of-health (SOH) estimation, while continuous SOC–SOH-dependent ECM parameter representation and validation of neural-network-inverted parameters remain limited. This study proposes an ECM-PINN framework that integrates a neural network with a differentiable first-order RC model for joint SOH estimation, ECM parameter inversion, and voltage reconstruction. An SOH-guided consistency regularization is introduced to regulate excessive cross-cell parameter dispersion. The framework is evaluated on the Samsung 50E and HUST datasets. On unseen Samsung 50E cells, the Pearson correlation coefficients between the inverted and conventionally identified R 0 , R 1 , and C 1 are 0.996, 0.998, and 0.992, respectively. On the HUST dataset, the SOH estimation MAE and RMSE are 0.53% and 0.74%, while the voltage reconstruction MAE and RMSE are 20.50 mV and 26.00 mV. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework can perform SOC–SOH-dependent ECM parameter inversion under both standardized HPPC and non-standard dynamic operating conditions, while maintaining stable SOH estimation and voltage reconstruction performance.

papers.title: Dual-time-scale predictive hierarchical electro-thermal coordination for thermal-load reshaping in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles
papers.abstract: Unlike passenger electric vehicles, heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles operate for long periods under high-load conditions. The continuous heat rejection of the engine-generator set through the engine high-temperature coolant loop makes fan/pump power directly interact with the direct-current (DC) bus power balance and generator–battery power split. Therefore, cooling power scheduling is part of energy management, rather than only a thermal-protection task. This paper proposes a dual-time-scale predictive hierarchical electro-thermal coordination strategy, termed DTP-HETC, for thermal-load reshaping in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles. A shared-encoder dual-head bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) predictor is used to capture short-horizon traction fluctuations and long-horizon engine-loop thermal evolution. The predicted thermal risk is quantified as thermal debt and converted into thermal buffer intensity B T k , which further adapts the thermal-load-shaping weights and the control-grid resolution of dynamic programming-based model predictive control (DP-MPC). By using this information, DTP-HETC advances part of the cooling effort from boundary-triggered response to thermal-risk formation intervals, smoothing cooling-induced DC-bus disturbances and coordinating fan/pump power with generator–battery power allocation. Simulation and hardware-in-the-loop tests on a 220-ton series hybrid mining truck show that, under sustained heavy-load uphill operation, DTP-HETC reduces equivalent fuel consumption by 12.16% and lowers peak engine-loop coolant temperature by 2.53 °C compared with a rule-based baseline. The mean execution time is 33.7 ms, confirming controller-level real-time feasibility. These results indicate that DTP-HETC provides an effective thermal-load reshaping approach for improving energy efficiency and thermal reliability in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles.

papers.title: Achieving Energy Efficiency in Building Heating and Cooling by Optimising Solar Energy-Based Control
papers.abstract: This paper examines the optimisation of control for a building heating and cooling system integrated with solar energy and a heat pump under the climatic conditions of Fergana Region. Solar irradiance G(t), outdoor air temperature T_a (t) and wind speed v_w (t) were included directly in the model as external disturbances. The model combines building thermal dynamics and wind dependence with electricity generation by the photovoltaic (PV) system and temperature-dependent heating and cooling models for the heat pump. The control problem was formulated as a model predictive control (MPC) method using a mathematical model and future weather forecasts; the objective function simultaneously minimised grid electricity use, deviations from the comfort temperature and frequent compressor changes. A representative year was constructed from monthly values obtained from open meteorological data for Fergana. Daily short-wave solar irradiation on a horizontal surface ranges from 2.0 to 8.0 kWh/m²·day, monthly mean air temperature from 0.6 to 28.3 °C, and mean wind speed from 1.48 to 3.17 m/s. For a 150 m² building equipped with a 6 kWp PV system and an 8 kW heat pump, model calculations showed that optimised control reduced the heat pump’s annual electricity consumption from 6,007 to 4,578 kWh, a reduction of 23.8%. papers.abstract: Abstract Prosthodontic education requires integration of theoretical knowledge, clinical judgment, and psychomotor skills. Conventional lectures and clinical demonstrations may provide limited opportunities for repeated practice before patient treatment. Simulation-based education, virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and gamification provide interactive alternatives that can enhance skill development and learner engagement. Simulation models such as phantom heads and jaw simulators allow students to practice procedures in a controlled environment. VR provides immersive clinical training, while AR integrates digital information with the real clinical field. Gamification incorporates game-based elements such as challenges, feedback, and rewards to promote active learning and motivation. The integration of these technologies can support progressive learning from theoretical knowledge to simulation and supervised clinical practice. Although limitations such as cost, technical requirements, training, and limited simulation of real clinical conditions exist, technology-assisted learning can serve as an effective complement to conventional prosthodontic education. Keywords: Prosthodontics; simulation; gamification; virtual reality; augmented reality; dental education; phantom head.

papers.abstract: This study aims to understand the effectiveness of the implementation of Ice Breaking in the form of Tepuk Salat (Praying Clapping) in overcoming learning boredom and increasing student activeness in the Fardhu Prayer material in Class II of Madrasah Ibtidaiyah (MI). Using a qualitative approach with a Selected Single Case Study design at MIN Semarang City, data were collected through in-depth interviews, non-active participant observation, and document analysis. The results showed that Ice Breaking was implemented in two phases, namely a refresher phase at the beginning of the lesson and a transition phase between materials. The findings of subjective meaning revealed that for teachers, Tepuk Salat functions as an active pause that prevents class boredom, while students interpret this activity as a fun game as well as a diversion from boredom. Significantly, student activeness increased, as seen from a decrease in disruptive behavior and an increase in participation in learning. These findings support the theory of active learning and student engagement, particularly through the mechanism of cognitive relaxation that recharges students' mental energy. Simple interventions such as Ice Breaking have proven effective in creating a dynamic classroom climate and supporting optimal mastery of the Fardhu Prayer procedural material. The implications of this research encourage the integration of contextual Ice Breaking in the Fiqh learning strategy in MI to improve the quality of the learning process.

papers.title: Assay Performance and Quantification Limits in Perioperative Serum Cytokine Measurement After Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Secondary Laboratory Analysis
papers.abstract: Background: Commercial cytokine assays may not span the concentrations encountered in perioperative serum. We examined the extent to which reconstructed enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay data from a total hip arthroplasty cohort could support temporal biological interpretation when most IL-6 and IL-10 results were below the validated quantification range. Methods: This post hoc secondary laboratory analysis used serum collected preoperatively and at 6, 24, and 48 h later from 44 of 52 participants in a single-centre three-arm trial. Five cytokines were measured by sandwich ELISA. Optical-density (OD) values were reconstructed from scanned reports and triangulated across three transcriptions. OD trajectories were summarised with within-patient rank tests as exploratory assay-signal observations. Five omnibus tests were Holm-adjusted across analytes. Detectability was analysed as a paired binary outcome using Cochran’s Q and exact McNemar comparisons with Holm correction. Clinical characteristics, acute-phase markers, and missing-data structure were evaluated in the assayed subcohort. Results: The assayed subcohort included all 18 no-block participants and 26 of 34 block recipients; the 8 non-assayed participants were late-enrolled block recipients. IL-6 OD varied over time (Friedman raw p = 2.6 × 10−11; Holm-adjusted p = 1.3 × 10−10), but 154/176 readings (87.5%) were below the LLOQ. IL-6 detectability was 0/44, 9/44, 7/44, and 6/44 at the four timepoints (Cochran Q = 12.27, p = 0.0065); only the preoperative-to-6 h McNemar comparison remained significant after correction (adjusted p = 0.023). TNF-alpha, IL-1alpha, and IL-10 OD also varied in exploratory analyses, whereas IL-1beta was inconclusive. CRP rose from a median 0.20 mg/dL preoperatively to 7.70 mg/dL at 24 h and 14.55 mg/dL at 48 h in the same 44 participants. Conclusions: The data document an assay-range and data-recovery problem more securely than they establish cytokine kinetics. The reconstructed OD changed systematically after surgery, especially for IL-6, but measurements below the validated range cannot establish concentration ordering, cross-cytokine dominance, or counter-regulation. Because re-assaying was not possible, all biological interpretations are presented as tentative and non-transferable. The reproducible findings are the extent of censoring, the limits of the available assay records, and the need to match the assay range to expected perioperative concentrations before clinical sampling.

papers.title: Navigation-Assisted and Robotic Total Hip, Knee, and Unicompartmental Arthroplasty: Reconciling Positioning Accuracy with Biomaterial Performance and Long-Term Implant Survival
papers.abstract: Navigation-assisted and robotic systems improve component positioning in total hip (THA), total knee (TKA), and unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA), but whether this improves biomaterial performance and implant survival is unclear. This structured narrative review asks for which bearing materials and fixation interfaces positioning accuracy plausibly alters the degradation and fixation pathways that govern survival, and how strong the evidence is for each link. We propose a conceptual model linking positioning to the local mechanical environment, material-specific degradation, biological response, and survival, and grade each link’s evidence by study design. Enabling technologies consistently reduce outliers. Position-dependent degradation is well documented for conventional polyethylene, ceramic-on-ceramic, and metal-on-metal bearings, mainly from simulator, retrieval, and cohort studies. Highly cross-linked polyethylene appears to attenuate the wear penalty of malposition, although rim fatigue and impingement remain position-sensitive and vitamin E stabilization has no proven additional clinical benefit. In cementless TKA, varus alignment is associated with greater early tibial migration, a validated surrogate for loosening. Clinical translation remains limited: trials and registries show no consistent reduction in all-cause revision after TKA or THA, with lower dislocation after THA and a more favorable UKA signal as exceptions. Precision may matter most for position-sensitive bearings and cementless interfaces.

papers.title: Metaheuristic Optimization of Temporal Surrogates for Early Prediction of Protein Conformational Stability from Short Molecular-Dynamics Trajectories
papers.abstract: Metaheuristic optimization can strengthen recurrent surrogates, but its value must be judged against controls and hyperparameter optimizers under leakage-free evaluation. We predict five equilibrium protein observables from 20ns prefixes of 100ns molecular-dynamics trajectories using a gated recurrent unit (GRU) configured by an Improved Grey Wolf Optimizer (Improved-GWO). The benchmark comprises 20 ATLAS proteins (60 trajectories) under nested leave-one-protein-out cross-validation. Relative to the original fixed GRU, Improved-GWO had lower absolute error for several observables; Holm-adjusted paired tests remained below 0.05 for SASA, helix and strand. Among six models, last-value persistence achieved the lowest nominal MAE for all five endpoints, and no persistence–Improved-GWO comparison survived Holm correction. A fixed 512-unit GRU improved nominally over the original small GRU, while paired tests favored Improved-GWO for helix and strand. In matched-budget HPO, Bayesian Optimization attained lower best inner-validation fitness than Improved-GWO, which in turn was lower than Random Search. Configurations from Random Search and Bayesian Optimization were not evaluated on outer tests. Ridge remained competitive. Thus, the benchmark does not establish a consistent predictive advantage from recurrent complexity over temporal or regularized linear baselines. The p53/NAMD assessment remains preliminary zero-shot evidence, and trajectory-length reduction is not a measured wall-clock speedup or validated stopping policy.
